events.feedback:
This draft for the Blue-gray Gnatcatcher (Polioptila caerulea) is excellent—it’s lively, easy to digest, and perfectly captures the frantic personality of this bird.

A critical review with an absolute zero-mistake lens reveals only one minor factual detail to adjust, along with a tiny formatting consistency check.

Factual Refinement
The Nesting Material (Microscopic Detail)
The Issue: Under "Quick Hits," the text states the nest is made of "bark fibers and plant down." While they do use some plant down, the primary structure of a gnatcatcher nest is built from shredded bark strip fibers and grass, bound with spider silk, and then decorated with lichen.

The Correction: To be 100% airtight, tweak "plant down" to "fine grasses" or just leave it as "shredded bark and grass."

Content & Layout Check
The Breeding Claim: The draft notes that pairs can build up to seven nests a season, and the "When to See It" section correctly notes that the individuals here in summer are our local breeder
events.summary: One targeted factual correction: the third Quick Hit now correctly identifies bark strips and grasses (not bark fibers and plant down) as the primary structural materials of the nest, matching Cornell Lab and multiple authoritative sources. All other fields are unchanged.
